title: fix(core): derive the undrawable list-view kinds instead of hard-coding them (objectui#9880)
body:
Fixes #9880

Clause-②: no — the exported `ListViewVisualization` resolves to the same nine members under either spec (compiled both ways below, and every downstream consumer re-compiled against the rebuilt declarations); no key on a published payload moves and no accept set is relaxed. What moves is how that type is DERIVED, plus a non-exported alias and table shape now visible in `@object-ui/core`'s emitted declaration.

## ⭐ The judgement the card asked for first: YES, a both-legs spelling exists

The card's first deliverable was the judgement, not a delete — and triage's mechanical re-grade switch (`pm:retriage` → `pm:on-hold`) was to be tripped only if a both-legs spelling were measurably impossible. It is not impossible, so the switch is **not** tripped and no re-grade is asked for.

**Why the old spelling could not survive the retirement.** Two literals were cited on the card; only ONE of them was ever a compile error, and this is a correction to the card's framing:

| site | old spelling | on the published leg | on the `main` leg |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| `ListViewVisualization` | `Exclude<ViewType, 'list' \| 'detail' \| 'page'>` | fine | **silently fine** — `Exclude` of a non-member is a no-op no compiler reads |
| `UNDRAWABLE_VIEW_KINDS` | annotated `Record<Exclude<ViewType, ListViewVisualization>, string \| null>` | fine | **TS2353** — the `page:` row is an excess property |

An annotated object literal is exact in BOTH directions. That is what makes the retirement unfixable under it: the addition direction wants a missing key to be an error (correct), and the retirement direction then makes a stale row an error too, whose only repair is deleting the row — which this repository cannot do while it resolves a published spec that still accepts `type: 'page'` views. The second literal was not a second error; it was a claim that had quietly stopped being true.

**The spelling that is total against both.** Keep the value constraint, drop the exactness, and derive the other half of the partition from the table's own keys intersected with the live vocabulary:

```ts
const UNDRAWABLE_VIEW_KINDS = {
  list: null,
  detail: null,
  page: 'it mounts a published page (bound through `pageName`) …',
} satisfies Record<string, string | null>;

type UndrawableViewKind = Extract<ViewType, keyof typeof UNDRAWABLE_VIEW_KINDS>;

export type ListViewVisualization = Exclude<ViewType, UndrawableViewKind>;
```

`Extract` is the load-bearing operator: a row for a kind the spec has RETIRED drops out of the type while staying live in the table at runtime, which is exactly what an author who can still write a `page` view against the resolved spec needs.

**The guard objectui#8127 installed is unchanged, it just lands in one place instead of two.** A kind the spec ADDS is classed by neither table, so it is not extracted, so it stays inside `ListViewVisualization` — and `LIST_VIEW_KINDS` is still a total `Record<ListViewVisualization, true>`, which goes red until the new kind is classed as drawable there or explained in the undrawable table. A MISSPELLED key in the undrawable table fails the same way, because the kind it was meant to class is not extracted either. ⛔ objectui#9860's gate is not weakened, narrowed or disabled anywhere in this diff; ⛔ the `@objectstack/spec` pin is untouched; ⛔ nothing here proposes reversing the upstream retirement.

## The two legs, compiled — same mechanism, same command

Injection is objectui#9877's own `scripts/spec-main-shape-gate.mjs inject` (remove-then-copy into pnpm's virtual store, `npm pack` bytes, 29 consumers verified), run from that branch's copy of the script; the script itself is **not** part of this diff. Command on every leg: `TURBO_FORCE=true pnpm exec turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/core --concurrency=2`, serialized behind the shared verify lock.

Readings taken 2026-09-18T18:20Z–18:35Z. objectui base `f5e2fcb4a` (`origin/main` at 2026-09-18T18:15Z, which had already moved past the `02bc27b08` this card was dispatched against). Injected spec built from `objectstack-ai/objectstack@07c6f822edd9c4c48a7ce34767de420c6096b9c3` (`origin/main` at 2026-09-18T18:19Z), packed as 2,039 files / 28,923,936 B.

| leg | spec resolved | source | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|:--|
| control | published `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` | before this change | exit 0 |
| subject | built from objectstack `07c6f822` | before this change | exit 2 — `src/utils/normalize-list-view.ts(205,3): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'page' does not exist in type 'Record<"list" \| "detail", string \| null>'` |
| control | published `@objectstack/spec@17.4.0` | **after** | exit 0 |
| subject | built from objectstack `07c6f822` | **after** | the TS2353 is **gone**; two diagnostics remain, both in OTHER files and both pre-existing (see below) |

The two vocabularies were read directly, so "both legs" is not an inference: the published spec's `ListViewSchema.shape.type` answers `["grid","kanban","gallery","calendar","timeline","gantt","map","chart","tree","page"]` and the `main`-built one answers the same list without `page`.

## ⚠️ This does NOT clear objectui#9860's day-one red, and the gate under-reports

⭐ **Measured, and it changes what objectui#9877 is waiting for.** With the `main`-built spec injected, `@object-ui/core` alone has **three** diagnostics, not one. The gate reported one because each package's `type-check` script is `tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`: the first half failed, so the TESTS project never ran. Running the tests project ALONE against the **pristine** (unchanged) source with `main`'s spec injected prints all three at once —

```
src/utils/__tests__/normalize-list-view.pageResidual-8429.test.ts(146,13): error TS2322: Type '"page"' is not assignable to type 'ViewType'.
src/utils/normalize-list-view.ts(205,3): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'page' does not exist in type 'Record<"list" | "detail", string | null>'.
src/validation/__tests__/object-validation-engine.test.ts(162,9): error TS2322: Property 'source' is missing in type '{ dialect: "cel"; ast: … }' …
```

— which is how the other two are proven to be pre-existing rather than introduced here (that control reverted this file by blob hash, ran, and restored by hash equality). Neither is this card's:

- the `pageResidual-8429` pin is the **deliberate tripwire** for objectui#8429: its own header says "narrow `ViewType` ⇒ the published faces stop accepting `page` ⇒ RED". It is red for the reason it was written to be red, and it cannot be made both-legs-total without deleting the thing it pins — its assertions (`SPEC_LIST_VIEW_TYPES.length` is 10, `ViewTypeSchema.safeParse('page').success` is true) are TRUE today on the published leg. It is a pin-bump conversion, not a repair.
- the `object-validation-engine` diagnostic is an unrelated upstream shape move (an expression wire that now requires `source`).

⇒ landing objectui#9877 still puts a red advisory check on every pull request. This diff removes one of the three reasons.

## Tests

New pin `packages/core/src/utils/__tests__/normalize-list-view.undrawableBothLegs-9880.test.ts`. Any single run installs only ONE spec, so the type-level half lifts the source's two operators over a SIMULATED vocabulary — published-shaped, `main`-shaped, and grown — and asserts the derived drawable set is the same under the first two, that a total record over it compiles under both, and that a grown vocabulary forces the new kind to be classed.

**The pins fire.** Ablating the two `@ts-expect-error` directives (mutation proven on disk by blob hash `f6189d5c…` → `7e392423…`, restored to `f6189d5c…` by hash equality, `trap` on EXIT/INT/TERM with absolute paths) makes `tsc -p packages/core/tsconfig.test.json` print exactly the two diagnostics they hold down, **on the published leg**, where the source itself cannot produce them:

```
…undrawableBothLegs-9880.test.ts(109,3): error TS2353: Object literal may only specify known properties, and 'page' does not exist in type 'Record<"list" | "detail", string | null>'.
…undrawableBothLegs-9880.test.ts(116,14): error TS2741: Property 'pivot' is missing in type '{ grid: true; kanban: true; }' but required in type 'Record<"grid" | "kanban" | "pivot", true>'.
```

The first is the card's own diagnostic, reproduced inside ordinary CI. One runtime assertion also needed a fresh module instance (`vi.resetModules()` + dynamic import): the undrawable warning is once-per-kind-per-module, and the `unit` project runs `isolate: false`, so a sibling suite in the same worker had already spent it — the first draft of that test failed for exactly that reason before it was corrected.

|:--|:--|
| `pnpm exec vitest run packages/core/` (published spec) | 156 files / 3295 tests passed |
| `turbo run type-check --filter=@object-ui/core` (published) | exit 0 |
| `turbo run type-check --filter=...@object-ui/core` (published, core + every downstream consumer) | exit 0 — 73 tasks |
| `turbo run build --filter=@object-ui/core` | exit 0 — declarations emit the derived type and the table shape |
| `node scripts/check-changeset-presence.mjs` | exit 0 — 1 published source file, 1 changeset |
| `node scripts/check-control-bytes.mjs` | exit 0 — 8005 tracked text files |
| `node scripts/check-new-cross-file-line-citations.mjs` | exit 0 — 0 new citations |
| `node scripts/check-type-check-coverage.mjs` | exit 0 — the new test file is compiled by `packages/core/tsconfig.test.json` |
| `node scripts/check-test-path-roots.mjs` · `node scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` | exit 0 |

| `node scripts/check-governed-queue-guard.mjs --test` on the 3 changed paths | exit 0 — NOT GOVERNED, 0 of 5 surfaces matched |

⚠️ **MEASURED AFTER this body was written, and the sentence that stood here — 「NOT MEASURED: a repo-wide `pnpm type-check` on the `main`-built leg」 — is replaced rather than left standing.** A repo-wide `TURBO_FORCE=true turbo run type-check --concurrency=3 --continue` against the `main`-built spec at objectstack `07c6f822` prints **20 unique diagnostics across 7 packages** — core 2, plugin-view 3, types 6, react 1, console 1, plus 7 cascade in `app-shell` and `example-byo-backend-console` from `plugin-view`'s failed build ⇒ **13 non-cascade across 5 packages**. `@object-ui/plugin-view` carries three more hard-coded `page` rows of exactly this card's class. ⭐ Without `--continue`, turbo cancels the dependents and the same census collapses to **1**. ⇒ this belongs to objectui#9877's decision and is carried there and on its own cards; it is recorded here because a reader of #9877 would otherwise use the replaced sentence to decide whether the gate's day-one break is cleared.

<sub>Body edited by the `domain:ui#2` execution seat at 2026-09-18T19:00Z (clock read by this write), on the dev's own hand-back and its recommendation A — a dev writes its PR body once and ⛔ never PATCHes it, so a falsified NOT-MEASURED claim is the seat's to repair. ⛔ Nothing else in this body was changed.</sub>

## Acceptance notes — out of scope, noted, not fixed here

- **The gate's break count is a lower bound, structurally.** Every package's `type-check` is `tsc && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so on a red leg the tests project never runs and its diagnostics never reach the annotation step. objectui#9877's "one file fails" is therefore an artifact of `&&`, not a census. Worth its own card against the gate. Dedupe words: `spec-main-shape-gate short-circuit tests project`, `type-check && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json masks diagnostics`.
- **`normalize-list-view.pageResidual-8429.test.ts` must be converted at the pin bump**, not repaired: it is single-leg BY CONSTRUCTION and red on `main` today. Dedupe words: `pageResidual 8429 pin ViewType narrowed`, `page residual conversion pin bump`.
- **`object-validation-engine.test.ts` expression-wire drift** — `{ dialect, ast }` without `source` no longer satisfies the spec's expression union on `main`. Unrelated file, unrelated mechanism. Dedupe words: `object-validation-engine dialect source expression wire`, `spec main expression requires source`.
- Noted, not filed: this file's `LIST_VIEW_KINDS` and the undrawable table are still two separate literals a reader must hold together; the partition is enforced, so this is ergonomics, and the carrier that would touch it is the pin-bump PR.
